prerequisites: Minimum knowledge of English is recommended for computer program usage and understanding some readings.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of industrial engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a team.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, its institutional and legal framework. Organization and management of companies.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Knowledge and skills to organize and manage projects. Understand the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Utilize digital simulation techniques as a tool for analyzing production and logistics systems.
Apply system modeling methods oriented to discrete events.
Use and know some of the most widely used simulation programs in both research and business.

syllabus_topics: Continuous, discrete, and discrete-event oriented systems.
Statistical simulation models. The Monte Carlo method.
Problem solving using simulation as an analysis tool. Validation of simulation models.
Construction of simulation models of production and/or logistics systems. Analysis of the bottleneck of a production line. Resource optimization.

assessment_methods.method: Punctual Control (CP1) - Written test on theoretical part (manual Monte Carlo simulation)
Punctual Control (CP2) - Practical test on building and validating a simple simulation model with Arena
Individual Tasks (TI) - Solving exercises using simulation with Excel and Arena
Final Individual Work (TIF) - Solving two cases using simulation, including documentation and public presentation

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the sum of CP1, CP2, and TI must have a minimum score of 1 point. The Final Individual Work (TIF) must have a minimum score of 2 points. If all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as NOTA = CP1 + CP2 + TI + TIF. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. In the extraordinary call, CP1 and CP2 scores are kept, Individual Tasks (TI) can be redone, and the Final Individual Work (TIF) must be submitted. For differentiated evaluation, students must submit the same individual/group works and present the individual work at the end of the course.
